notes:
Summary: FluxShield builds a multichannel CX platform used by several retail and fintech customers. Primary pain: spikes (product launches, Black Friday-like campaigns) cause long live-agent queues and cascading downstream system failures. They want a solution that keeps agent-assist and automated reply tooling usable during 5x–10x bursts for 5–15 minutes without dropping context or escalating token costs.

Requirements (from meetings):
- Workload: real-time agent assist + automated triage + ticket summarization + tool-calling (CRM patch, triage macros). Also embeddings for semantic search / reranking of KB.
- SLA targets: p95 response latency for agent-assist generation <= 350ms for short prompts (~50–150 tokens); throughput baseline 1500 req/min sustained, must absorb 5x peak bursts (7500 req/min) for 10 minutes with >=99% success.
- Availability: regional failover (NA + EU), data residency for EU tenant data, audit logs retained 1 year for enterprise customers.
- Cost sensitivity: wants cost-per-1k-token target to stay under current internal gateway cost; looking to quantify Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
- Integration: existing CTI, message bus (Kafka), and agent desktop (custom). Need function/tool calling for CRM writes and macro triggers.
- Backpressure policy: prefer graceful degradation (switch to retrieval-only responses or shorter-model variant) vs 429s; must never silently drop tool-calls.

POC plan and success criteria (agreed):
- 3-week POC: week 1 integration + baseline, week 2 sustained-load tests, week 3 synthetic-burst chaos runs (5x, 10x).
- Redwood to provide: Dedicated pool config, warm-standby scaling policy, routing policies for model variants, batching/caching settings, cost dashboard.
- Success metrics: under POC burst scenario (5x for 10 min): p95 latency < 500ms and error rate < 1.5%; agent-assist token cost delta <= 30% vs baseline; correct tool-call success >= 99.5%.
- Additional checks: KV/prefix cache behavior across session reconnects; streaming reliability for multi-step tool-calling; ability to route to fallback model when higher-tier capacity saturated.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If the assist goes slow during launches, our agents abandon the chat and conversion tanks. We need predictable behavior under chaos, not just average numbers." — Sr. Ops lead
- "We cannot accept opaque failures. Audit trail for every automated CRM write is mandatory." — Head of Security

Technical asks / config details they requested:
- Warm pools with preloaded KV cache for commonly used customer contexts (cart, order history).
- Canary rules: route 10% to smaller quantized variant during bursts to preserve throughput.
- Backpressure signals from Redwood to FluxShield's message bus (HTTP webhook + Kafka) to throttle new session creation.
- Function-calling guarantee: idempotency tokens and exactly-once semantics for CRM writes; retriable responses with hooks.

Blockers: security questionnaire outstanding (data residency clarifications), estimate to procure dedicated GPUs (finance/commitments), CTI glue work ambiguous (FluxShield devs to deliver adapter).

Next steps (short): run Redwood proof-of-load (scheduled 2026-03-15), security follow-up (Carlos), finalize SOW draft (Maya) by 2026-03-25.
